definition: PMT usually refers to Protection Motivation Theory, a psychology framework for understanding willingness to take protective action. In this packet, it describes how perceived severity, perceived vulnerability, response efficacy, self-efficacy, and response cost may shape a person’s motivation to get vaccinated.

reasons: The definition includes an unsupported general claim that “PMT usually refers to Protection Motivation Theory” and describes it as a general “psychology framework,” but the packet only uses PMT within a specific study context (male HPV vaccination willingness).

While the packet does support that the model includes perceived severity, perceived vulnerability, response efficacy, self-efficacy, and response cost as PMT cognitions shaping vaccination willingness, it does not support the broader phrasing about “willingness to take protective action” beyond vaccination willingness in this study.
The definition’s vaccination-focused phrasing (“may shape a person’s motivation to get vaccinated”) is supported in this packet, but the added generalizations about PMT’s typical meaning are not.
